key_insight: Staged knowledge distillation turns visual quantum reinforcement learning into a compact-head learning problem, letting shallow quantum-compatible policies learn from a frozen classical visual teacher instead of training end-to-end from pixels.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path for deploying small VQC-based controllers in visual control tasks where full quantum RL pipelines are too unstable, data-hungry, or expensive to train.
method: Train a classical visual teacher on pixel observations.
Freeze the teacher encoder and use it as a fixed feature interface.
Distil teacher policy behavior into compact downstream heads, either classical or VQC-based.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on CartPole Pixels and Acrobot Pixels, where staged KD enabled shallow VQC heads to achieve non-trivial control; angle encoding stayed near teacher performance while amplitude encoding achieved extreme compactness.
watch_item: Amplitude-encoded VQC heads appear more fragile and budget-sensitive, with higher simulation cost, so hardware and runtime constraints may limit practical use.
paper_title: Staged Hybridisation for Visual Quantum Reinforcement Learning via Knowledge Distillation
